title: spillway r14: faithful cs bhop and wide playable comparisons
description:
/goal Spillway R14: real CS:GO-style bhop and air strafing, explored wide. Mike played R13 Overflow. His verdict: he is still expecting CS:GO movement and air strafing, and what he gets is momentum he cannot control or keep when he strafes in the air. Bounded W/mouse steering is not the feel he wants. He is going off to play actual CS bhop servers to scratch the itch, so that is the reference he will judge against when he comes back. This round is for experimenting wildly and spreading wide: budget is not a concern, delegate freely, run parallel variants in their own worktrees, be bold, have fun.

What he wants to end up with:
1. A faithful Source/CS:GO movement model as the baseline, reimplemented from the public cvars and the well-known PM_Accelerate / PM_AirAccelerate / PM_Friction behaviour (no copied engine code): ground accelerate and friction with stopspeed, the 30-unit air wishspeed cap, sv_airaccelerate, gravity 800 and the CS:GO jump impulse, converted to Godot units with the conversion written down. Strafing with A/D while turning the mouse the same way must hold and build speed exactly the way a CS player expects, and letting go must keep the line. Check it against known CS numbers (for example the gain per well-synced strafe at a given airaccelerate, and max speed from a standing start after N hops), not only internal tests.
2. Several movement presets switchable in game without restarting, so Mike can compare in one sitting: at least CS:GO vanilla (airaccelerate 12), CS:GO bhop server (airaccelerate 100, autohop, no stamina), and R13 Overflow as it is; add any others you think are worth his time (Quake/CPMA air control, a VHOLUME-inspired one, your own). Show the active preset on screen.
3. A strafe HUD like bhop servers have: speed, gain or loss per jump, strafe sync percentage, so he can tell whether a bad hop was him or the physics.
4. An original bhop practice map beside the dam course: blocks, strafe-around corners, gaps that need real speed, a long straight to build speed. Original layout, not a copy of any existing map. The Spillway course stays playable with every preset.

Keep everything else from the R13 workflow: honest evidence, scripted input traces, packed checks run outside the source checkout, portable Linux and Windows ZIPs in delivery/spillway-r14/, REPORT.md telling him how to play and switch presets, commits pushed to feat/foldrunner-me-build with (ccChat-general-rowb) in the subject. Do not claim it feels right; he decides that. Work until at least 20:00 Europe/Prague today, Sunday 8 Nov 2026, and keep improving what is actually playable rather than stopping at a test count. Mike is away: decide everything yourself and label it, never stop to ask.
acceptance_criteria: Faithful original Source/CS:GO movement checked against independent external numbers; hot-switchable vanilla AA12, bhop AA100/autohop/no-stamina and unchanged R13 plus worthwhile variants; active preset and speed/jump-gain/sync HUD; original bhop practice map and playable Overflow in every preset; native/input evidence, isolated packed checks, Linux/Windows ZIPs in delivery/spillway-r14, current REPORT and coherent pushed rowb commits. Continue actual playable improvement until at least 20:00 Europe/Prague Sunday 8 November 2026. Human feel unverified until Mike judges it.

dependencies.title: foldrunner: reverse-engineer mirror's edge movement and camera into a godot spec (codex goal on the laptop)
dependencies.description:
runs on: laptop (the brief, the tools and the game files live there; the desktop goes off overnight and Windows is Mike's gaming boot).

Mike, 4 Nov 2026: both Foldrunner rebuilds of 3 Nov missed the feel. The Opus one was more polished and closer to Mirror's Edge but had less momentum; the GPT one was faster, but its momentum felt like Clustertruck. His idea: copy his own Mirror's Edge onto the laptop and have GPT reverse-engineer the game's movement and camera, using REA (github.com/morluto/rea, npm `rea-agents`, "Reverse Engineer Anything": an MCP and CLI over Ghidra, Hopper or IDA, .NET and JS analysis). The folding world stays original; Control Resonant is not reverse-engineered. The output is a numeric spec that a second goal (the follow-up bead) builds Foldrunner's movement from.

Spec: `/home/thatmike1/mirrors-edge-re/BRIEF.md` on the laptop. The launch message is `goal.txt` next to it (a Codex `/goal`, no time limit). Artifact: `/home/thatmike1/mirrors-edge-re/SPEC.md` plus `evidence/`, all of it staying on the laptop. Stops when the spec covers the brief's list as far as the files allow. No commits, no deploy.

How to launch (Mike starts it from Windows in the evening by telling an instance to do it):

1. **Find the game.** On Windows, find the installed Mirror's Edge folder: Steam, EA app or GOG. It holds `Binaries\` and `TdGame\`.
2. **Check the connection.** The Windows boot has an SSH key the laptop already accepts (authorized_keys comment `windows-desktop->laptop`). The laptop is `thatmike1@omarchy.local` (avahi; it was 192.168.0.179 on 20 Oct), and the Windows `~/.ssh/config` may have an alias for it. Check with `ssh thatmike1@omarchy.local "df -h /home"`: about 17 GB was free on 4 Nov and the game is about 8 GB.
3. **Copy the folder.** Use `scp -r "<install folder>" thatmike1@omarchy.local:/home/thatmike1/` and then, on the laptop, rename the result to `/home/thatmike1/mirrors-edge`. Do not pipe tar through PowerShell: its pipes can corrupt binary data. `TdGame\Movies` (Bink videos) can be skipped to save space.
4. **Verify it.** Compare the file count and total size on both ends.
5. **Launch it on the laptop's T3:**
   `ssh thatmike1@omarchy.local`, then
   `export PATH=$HOME/.local/share/mise/shims:$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH; J=/home/thatmike1/mirrors-edge-re; t3 project add $J --title "mirrors edge re"; python3 ~/.local/share/t3-cli/t3ctl.py launch $J codex high "mirrors edge: movement spec" $J/goal.txt`.
   It prints the thread id (gpt-6.1-sol, high).
6. **Check it started.** `python3 ~/.local/share/t3-cli/t3ctl.py status <thread-id>` should print `running`. `sqlite3 ~/.codex/goals_1.sqlite "select status from thread_goals order by rowid desc limit 1"` should print `active`.
7. **Record it.** Comment the thread id on this bead, claim it, and run `bd sync`.

Notes for the run, already in the brief:
- **Tools:** Ghidra, a JDK and a .NET SDK are not installed. The agent installs them into `tools/` without sudo. dotnet runtime 10, node 26 and procps are present.
- **Approach:** Unreal Engine 3 keeps most gameplay in UnrealScript packages, so UE Explorer or UELib decompiles them, and REA with Ghidra covers native code.
- **Privacy:** game files and decompiled code never get committed or uploaded.
